entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים names the God in whose image humankind was made, recalling Genesis 1:27.

review.translation: [Whoever sheds|0] [the blood of|1] [a human being|2], [by a human being|3] [his blood|4] [shall be shed|5], [because|6] [in the image of|7] [God|8] [he made|9] [humankind|11,10].

analysis.evidence: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם means “whoever sheds human blood.” The following clause דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed,” echoes the verb in the passive and confirms the bloodshed sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, with no prefix or suffix. It functions substantivally and takes דַּם הָאָדָם as its object.

analysis.evidence: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם means “one who sheds human blood.” The answering clause דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed,” holds the killer accountable for the death.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with הָאָדָם as its genitive complement.
analysis.sense: Bloodshed in the taking of a human life.

analysis.evidence: In שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם, “whoever sheds the blood of a human being,” הָאָדָם identifies the person whose blood is shed. The rule applies to any human victim.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun. The article is generic here.
analysis.sense: a man, a human being; anyone

analysis.evidence: In בָּאָדָם דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “by a human being his blood shall be shed,” בָּאָדָם identifies the human agent who sheds the blood of the person described in the opening clause.
analysis.morphology: The prefix בָּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article. אָדָם is a masculine singular absolute noun. The article is generic here.
analysis.sense: a man, a human being; anyone

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:6 as evidence for the existing bloodshed and responsibility sense.
draft.definition: Human lifeblood shed in connection with a violent death. Here the killer answers for the death with his own blood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:6 pairs שֹׁפֵךְ, “whoever sheds,” with דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed.”

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers back to שֹׁפֵךְ, “whoever sheds.” The opening clause names the victim’s blood as the object of shedding. In דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed,” the killer’s own blood is the subject of the passive verb.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ, “his.”
analysis.sense: The killer’s own lifeblood, to be shed in recompense for the life he took.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs active שֹׁפֵךְ ‘one who sheds’ with passive יִשָּׁפֵךְ ‘shall be shed’. The subject of the passive verb is דָּמוֹ ‘his blood’, the blood of the person who shed human blood.
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with דָּמוֹ ‘his blood’. The initial י marks the imperfect, and the Niphal נ assimilates to שׁ.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the preceding judgment about shedding human blood: God made humankind in his image.
analysis.morphology: Causal conjunction without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים modifies עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם, “he made humankind.” The phrase identifies God as the one whose likeness humankind bears.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The masculine singular noun צֶלֶם stands in construct with אֱלֹהִים.

analysis.evidence: In בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים, “in the image of God,” אֱלֹהִים completes the construct phrase. The singular verb עָשָׂה, “he made,” refers to God as the one who made humankind.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with a singular referent.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָדָם (humankind) as the direct object of עָשָׂה. The phrase בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים (in the image of God) describes how God made humankind, establishing the creation sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the direct object of עָשָׂה. God made humankind in his image, and the כִּי clause gives this as the reason the rule applies to anyone who sheds human blood.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
